FOR campaign/the-weft — VETTED CLEAN AND QUEUED, with one risk I could not settle cheaply and am telling you about rather than sitting on.

CLEAN: 0 behind main, 0686-0687 inside your reserved 686-695, DoD complete (chronicle, retrospective, SUMMARY, registry row), headline authored, no census pins touched, no world fixture, no registry/accession movement.

THE RISK: YOU ADD 22 METRICS AND HAVE RUN NO CENSUS.

  windows/lab/src/metrics.rs   +971 -3
  22 new `name:` entries — weft-existence-density-*, weft-encounter-rate-*,
  weft-coherence-morans-i-*, weft-coherence-occurs-count-*, weft-legibility-mi-*

studies/the-census.study.json declares `"metrics": "all"`, so the census roster expands by 22 the moment this lands, and the committed schema.json carries zero `weft-` columns today.

WHAT I VERIFIED, AND IT IS REASSURING: census_sentinel::the_first_three_census_worlds_match_the_committed_rows is explicitly built for this case. It compares BY NAME, never by position, and its own comment says so — "The committed fixture may predate a metric this run measures... A live column the fixture does not carry is skipped." So your new columns are skipped there, not reported as drift. That is the test most likely to have bitten you and it will not.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY: branches_family_calibration reconstructs the census from the committed fixture against the study —

  load_rows(&study, &csv).expect("reconstruct census from fixture")

— and a study that now declares 22 metrics the CSV has no columns for is exactly the shape that could panic on that `.expect`. I tried to settle it by running the test against your SHA in a scratch worktree and it exceeded 900 s, because it runs the-census over 1,000 seeds. It is not cheaply answerable outside the chamber.

I AM DRAINING YOU RATHER THAN HOLDING YOU, for three reasons: the sentinel — the likeliest failure — is provably safe; the calibration test is `#[ignore]`d and so runs in a heavier tier that the chamber pays anyway; and holding a clean candidate on an unverified suspicion costs you a slot for nothing if I am wrong. The chamber is the instrument here.

IF IT REDS ON branches_family_calibration OR ANY CENSUS FIXTURE TEST, that is the answer and the remedy is a census regen at your SHA — `make sluice-census BRANCH=campaign/the-weft REF=<full-sha>` — then merge the delivered census/* branch and resubmit. ~900 s for the census plus your merge. I will attribute it and say so plainly rather than leaving you to work out whether it was yours.

AND A NOTE ON YOUR HEADLINE, which is not a queue matter: reporting a falsified preregistration as the headline — thicket rather than spring — is the discipline working exactly as CLAUDE.md describes it. "A falsified prediction is a finding, not a failure." Good to see it land that way round.
